brief: A public drinking-water utility operations workspace helps field crews and control-room dispatchers respond to burst mains and planned outages across three districts. Teams need to locate affected streets, assign qualified repair crews, verify isolation and water-quality clearance before service returns, and prepare accessible resident updates. Technicians use phones with intermittent connectivity. This is an offline product prototype with sample data only.

ASSUMPTIONS TO REVIEW
Your brief points to: Public Water Operations.
Likely audience: Network controllers, water-quality reviewers, field technicians, dispatchers, and resident communications teams.
Main goal: Restore public water service safely by coordinating network incidents, controlled isolation, qualified repairs, documented water-quality clearance, and accessible outage updates.
Team collaboration is central to these workflows.
Mobile use matters, so touch-friendly controls are included.
The design uses your feel words: “calm, precise, and reassuring”.

Triage a water service interruption and dispatch a qualified repair crew

Review the service report and verify the affected network asset → Confirm the affected streets and the current service impact → Assign a crew with the required recorded competencies → Verify isolation and record repair progress against the work order

YESTERDAY
Review water quality evidence before returning service

Record the sampling location, collection time, and approved test method → Route results to an authorised water quality reviewer → Record the evidence, decision, reviewer, and timestamp → Return service only after the responsible utility confirms its clearance procedure

EARLIER THIS WEEK
Prepare an accessible update for residents in an affected area

Confirm the affected area and describe the known service impact → State the next update time without inventing a restoration estimate → Check accessible and translated formats required by the utility → Submit the notice to an authorised communications reviewer
